g.text: Epoch-based reclamation — defer the free until old-epoch readers depart (no use-after-free)
Reader A enters and pins the current epoch
native speed and may hold a raw `*const Node`
into the victim. The SeqCst pin publishes
BEFORE any pointer A subsequently loads.
Eviction thread opens an epoch boundary
wait_for_quiescence: the SeqCst load pairs with A's
SeqCst pin (StoreLoad fence). If the scan misses A,
A is guaranteed to observe the unlink and re-fault —
AcqRel alone would NOT close this gap.
Slow path: block on the quiescence condvar
Reader A is still walking the victim subtree
Reader A finishes and leaves the epoch
A's pointer accesses are globally ordered
BEFORE this un-pin, so a reclaimer that now
sees the count hit 0 knows A is done.
Quiescent: now the swap + free are safe
Ok(old_ptr) — the in-memory node is unlinked
No live reader can still reach it.
A reader that arrives AFTER the boundary is always safe
preceded the free) and faults the node back in from
disk — it never touches the freed allocation.
advance → wait for quiescence → swap → free.
The free is delayed until no thread from the pre-boundary epoch can hold a
pointer to the victim, which is exactly what lets eviction run concurrently
